_comment: Robot layout for v4_s1_v4_lh (COOHAVIOR's S1-V4-LH), ported to Merom_1_int.

Teams are team_1.. in order of appearance and robots are <type>_<team ordinal> (user, 2026-09-13; unified across every S1 layout). The V4 set a team came from (M5, M3, ...) survives only in each robot's _v4_prim.
LH stages exactly the same three robots at the same station as LL -- the
audit index's M5 set, poses identical to the last decimal. Two things differ.
The destination: LL puts the cargo on the bedroom floor, LH puts it on a
bedroom cabinet, so the last action is place_on_top onto furniture rather
than onto the ground.
And the weight. COOHAVIOR/behavior_style_task/tasks.modified.json sets box_mass_kg 0.008 for LL
and HL, 0.02 for LH and HH, under the one name packing_box.n.02_N, so
nothing symbolic could tell them apart. Here the two weights are two
0.02 kg for the heavy tasks, dice-iswudu at 0.008 for the light ones. LH is
heavy, so its cargo is notebook.n.01_1.
The cabinet is bound by the activity to cabinet.n.01_1. Which cabinet that
is is drawn per sample and is not stable: bedroom_0 holds four and `inroom`
binds by room *type*. Two guards make that safe rather than silent -- the
sampler refuses to remove anything the BDDL bound to (one draw picked a
cabinet in V4's own deactivation list), and it asserts the bound object
actually *stands* in bedroom_0 by the seg map rather than trusting the
scene's in_rooms annotation, which for bottom_cabinet_jrhgeu_1 says bedroom
while the object is in the child's room.
The three models are deliberately unequal, which is the point of the task:
only the Ridgeback's UR5 and the Crazyflie's belly suction cup can grasp.
The Jackal has no arm at all -- navigate_to and wait, nothing more -- and
V4 uses it as a carrier. ridgeback_1 is base-locked while holding, which V4
states on its own Ridgeback prim (v4:base_locked_while_holding, present on
all five of them). It can pick the cargo up but not carry it, so the route to
the bedroom is through jackal_1, the carrier. NOT through the drone: per
COOHAVIOR/behavior_style_task/tasks.modified.json's execution contract the
Crazyflie 'is not a load-bearing role for the 20 g box', and the heavy
packages require pull_car + push_car + robot_arm together. That constraint
That constraint is enforced by the route file's `lift` table (2026-09-12):
route.json says notebook.n.01 may be lifted by [arm] only, and `"drone":
true` here is what makes drone_2 a drone for that table. The engine
refuses its grasp with CANNOT_LIFT and the listing shows it `blocked [too
heavy for you]` -- see ROUTE_SUPERVISION_PLAN.md section 5.4.
SCALES ARE THE ONES v4_s1_v4_ll WAS VERIFIED WITH, NOT V4'S OWN. The
staging USD says jackal 0.5, ridgeback_franka 1.0, Crazyflie 0.6 (now 2.0, see below); the LL
layout and PORTING_COOHAVIOR.md both say 'Ridgeback 0.5, Jackal 0.7,
Crazyflie 0.6 (now 2.0, see below), read off xformOp:scale', and two of those three do not match
the file. Kept as LL has them rather than quietly changed. Unresolved.
Two teams, so chain and centralized have inter-team traffic to carry;
individual ignores the split.
Dice and Crazyflie are at scale 2.0 -- twice native -- by decision (user,
2026-09-12), and every later port keeps that: a 1.8 cm die and a 12 cm drone
were too small to see or to reason about at room scale. The drone's 2.0
replaces the 0.6 above; the dice's 2.0 is set in the sampler whitelist and
baked into the cached instance, so a re-sample is needed to change it.
